Word-by-word diff: only the object changes ("it the same" becomes "the Nurturer voice"); "I'd still keep" is intact, so the voice marker and the author's hedged recommendation survive. Nothing is lost and no claim is added: "it the same" meant the voice already named two paragraphs up ("the same Nurturer voice you meant for your little one"), and the draft says so by name. In context the paragraph reads "A harder voice can seem more fitting for something that's been in your way. I'd still keep the Nurturer voice. If that voice isn't there in you yet, borrow it from someone who's been safe for you." This is exactly what the_change describes: after "a harder voice", the old "it the same" and the next sentence's "that voice" could point at the harder one; now "that voice" follows a named Nurturer voice and can only mean it. "Nurturer voice" matches the section's own usage ("the role of the Nurturer"), so no new term, fact or first-person claim (C01-C04 absent; the "I'd" is the source's).
